intent: Replace Super price and daily carousels with one exclusive product for exact 12-hour and 24-hour display windows; preserve weekly carousel. Catalog windows are deterministic fixed durations from 2026-01-01T00:00:00+02:00 and keep fallback products distinct when possible. Preserve paid booking durations and prevent overlapping pending/active Super price bookings without deleting or repricing data; refresh selections at expiry.

findings.first_evidence: src/lib/catalog-offers.ts:45 --   const superOffer = superPool.length ? superPool[halfDay % superPool.length] : daily;
findings.suggested_fix: Select each half-day slot from a stable catalog order while excluding that day’s daily product and the previous slot’s Super price product when at least three distinct products are available. Add a three-product regression covering the second-half-day to next-day boundary.
findings.title: Avoid repeating Super price across consecutive windows
findings.why_it_matters: With three eligible products, the Super price card repeats across the overnight boundary and remains the same product for 24 hours while its countdown resets. For example, one-brand products 1/2/3 select product 3 at both 2026-11-03 12:00 +02 and 2026-11-04 00:00 +02, despite another product being available and the UI promising a new selection when the display period ends. Coordinating the half-day selection with the daily ordering avoids consecutive duplicates while preserving distinct daily and Super price cards.
findings.validation_reason: With three eligible products under one brand and no paid Super price, the frozen catalogOfferSelections function reproduces product 3 in both the November 3 noon and November 4 midnight windows with different ends_at values; the new halfDay indexing and daily rotation introduce this reachable contradiction of PromotedOffers.tsx:65, although production incidence was not measured.

findings.title: Exercise expiry refresh through the rendered promotions component
findings.why_it_matters: The central promise that a new product appears at expiry has no executable coverage. The added unit tests call only catalogOfferSelections, so they still pass if the new expiry fetch is removed or the expired ExclusiveOffer stays blank. A component or browser test with a controlled clock must exercise the actual timer and returned replacement, including cleanup when the view unmounts.
findings.validation_reason: The diff adds expiry-triggered loading and ExclusiveOffer lifecycle behavior in PromotedOffers.tsx:18-40 and 90-97, but inspection of tests finds only pure catalog-selection assertions and API tests, so the reachable mounted-component expiry/refresh path has no executable coverage; production incidence is inapplicable to this coverage gap.

triage_groups.title: Make twelve-hour rotation observable
triage_groups.context: The selector and its rendered expiry transition jointly implement the promised replacement.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Fix consecutive-window selection in #1, then add the rendered boundary coverage in #2.
triage_groups.why: A correct selection alone does not verify that an open page replaces its card.

residual_risks: The new exclusion constraint validates every pending/active Super price row, including intervals that already ended. The supplied zero-upcoming-bookings check does not establish that historical pending/active intervals are disjoint. Before rollout, inspect all overlapping pairs with SELECT a.id,b.id FROM public.promotions a JOIN public.promotions b ON a.id<b.id AND tstzrange(a.starts_at,a.ends_at,'[)') && tstzrange(b.starts_at,b.ends_at,'[)') WHERE a.type='super_pret' AND b.type='super_pret' AND a.status IN ('pending','active') AND b.status IN ('pending','active'); any result intentionally blocks this migration under its preservation policy. Production data was unavailable to this read-only frozen review.
